story.title: Ebola Outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo Claims Over 5,000 Lives
story.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in more than 5,000 deaths, according to government data. Additionally, over 10,000 individuals have contracted the virus during this outbreak, marking it as one of the deadliest in the region's history.

timeline_highlights.title: Congolese Politician Beaten After Promoting Ebola Awareness
timeline_highlights.summary: Marie-Celestin Karondwa, a politician from the ruling UDPS party in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, was beaten on Sunday after advocating for Ebola awareness during a radio interview. The incident occurred in Butembo, a region experiencing an Ebola outbreak, as residents reacted violently to his message promoting disease prevention measures.
key_facts: Marie-Celestin Karondwa was a member of the UDPS party.
He was attacked after a radio interview about Ebola awareness.
The incident took place in Butembo, North Kivu province.

timeline_highlights.title: Ebola Outbreak in DR Congo Surpasses 10,000 Cases Amid Growing Concerns
timeline_highlights.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has exceeded 10,000 confirmed cases, with nearly 4,900 reported deaths. This outbreak, driven by the Bundibugyo virus, is noted as the fastest-growing in history, raising alarms about potential spread to other African nations. Currently, there are no approved vaccines or specific treatments available for this strain of the virus.
key_facts: Over 10,000 confirmed Ebola cases in DR Congo.
Nearly 4,900 deaths reported.
Outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus.
No approved vaccines or specific treatments available.

timeline_highlights.title: Last Ebola Patients Depart Treatment Center in DR Congo
timeline_highlights.summary: A treatment center in Ituri province, DR Congo, celebrated the discharge of its last confirmed Ebola patients, marking the first time since May that the facility has had no active cases. Medical staff and local residents participated in a joyful celebration as the clinic, run by Médecins Sans Frontières, reached this significant milestone.
key_facts: Last confirmed Ebola patients discharged from a treatment center in Ituri province, DR Congo.
The clinic has had no confirmed cases since the outbreak was declared in May.
Celebration involved medical staff and local residents.

related_stories.title: BJP Criticizes Opposition's Mock Parliament and Challenges Gandhi to Debate
related_stories.summary: The BJP has criticized the opposition's mock Parliament initiative, with MP Sambit Patra suggesting that Rahul Gandhi should be made a 'mock PM.' Patra dismissed the opposition's allegations of electoral fraud, citing that similar events occurred during Congress rule. Additionally, Home Minister Amit Shah has challenged Gandhi to debate the allegations of vote theft in Parliament, coinciding with an upcoming opposition rally in Delhi.

related_stories.title: UK Prime Minister Open to Slavery Apology Amid Caribbean Tour
related_stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has expressed openness to a formal apology for Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade. This statement comes as King Charles continues his tour of the Caribbean, where discussions about the UK's colonial history are prominent. However, Burnham has ruled out the possibility of financial reparations, despite ongoing demands from Caribbean nations.
